subject: math

objective.text: Use drawings of equal groups and repeated addition. Use doubles to add faster.

explanations.title: Add one group at a time
explanations.text: 4 groups of 4 is 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4. Add one group at a time. 4 plus 4 is 8. 8 plus 4 is 12. 12 plus 4 is 16.

explanations.title: Use doubles to bundle groups
explanations.text: Pair the groups. 4 plus 4 is 8. Then there is another 4 plus 4, which is 8. 8 plus 8 is 16. So 4 groups of 4 is the same as 2 groups of 8.

explanations.title: Skip-count to add
explanations.text: You can skip-count to add equal groups. For 4 groups of 5, count 5, 10, 15, 20. The total is 20.

explanations.title: Same total, new groups
explanations.text: 4 groups of 5 and 2 groups of 10 have the same total, 20. You only group the circles in a new way. Each group of 10 has 2 fives.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (4 groups of 5 and 2 groups of 10)

explanations.title: Pair the addends, then add on the extra
explanations.text: Group the addends in pairs and use doubles. If one addend is left over, add it on at the end. 5 twos is 4 plus 4 plus 2, which is 10.

examples.title: 4 groups of 4
examples.text: 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4. Pair them: 8 plus 8 equals 16. 4 groups of 4 equals 2 groups of 8.

examples.title: 4 groups of 5
examples.text: 5 plus 5 plus 5 plus 5. Add one at a time: 10, 15, 20. Use doubles: 10 plus 10 equals 20. Skip-count: 5, 10, 15, 20.

examples.title: 6 groups of 3
examples.text: 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3. Pair them to make 6 plus 6 plus 6. 6 plus 6 is 12. 12 plus 6 is 18.

examples.title: 5 groups of 2
examples.text: 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2. Pair them to make 4 plus 4 plus 2. 4 plus 4 is 8. 8 plus 2 is 10.
